articles.title_orig: Inside India newsletter: New Delhi approves $22 billion in military spending amid China border tensions
articles.title_zh: Inside India newsletter: New Delhi approves $22 billion in military spending amid China border tensions
articles.content_orig:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
Welcome to the latest edition of " Inside India " — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
India, the world's fifth-largest military spender, shares a contentious relationship with two of its nuclear-armed neighbors — China and Pakistan. Last year, New Delhi carried out military strikes against alleged terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan, and last week an Indian official confirmed some border clashes with China.
As tensions at its borders simmer, India this week announced plans to spend billions of dollars on procuring modern warfare equipment. From whom will it get the goods?
Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.
The world's second-largest arms importer, India, is pouring billions of dollars into modernizing its military as it seeks to counter the technological advancements of neighboring China, with whom it shares an uneasy peace.
Last week, an Indian military official said that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's north-eastern border.
Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, the director general of a division of India's central armed forces, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, also called China the "biggest adversary" and urged for modernization of defense equipment. "It will be difficult to compete with China using traditional methods," Kapoor said.
Following Kapoor's comments, India approved spending 2.12 trillion rupees ($22 billion) to modernize its defense equipment on Monday. The country plans to spend on long-range kamikaze drones, surveillance and strike systems, counter-drone technologies, short-range air defense, artillery, helicopters and naval platforms.
Experts told CNBC that New Delhi increasingly views Beijing as a threat, especially given the Sino-Pakistan military ties, and the latest purchases were aimed at bridging the technological gap with China.
A spokesperson for India's foreign ministry said on Friday that "the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns." Beijing responded, saying it "strictly abides by the relevant agreements and common understandings reached between the two countries."
India's military policies are largely driven by its long-standing conflict with Pakistan, and an "increasing perception of China as a threat," Pieter Wezeman, senior researcher at the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, told CNBC.
According to a SIPRI report earlier this year, 61% of Chinese arms exports were supplied to Pakistan between 2021 and 2025.
India's latest weapons purchases will involve importing components and technology from South Korea for the artillery, engines and avionics from France for the helicopters, and drones from the U.S. and Israel, Wezeman said.
Collaboration with Russia and Japan could also be on the cards, given India's need for a technological upgrade.
Since April, India has greenlighted military spending totaling 3.7 trillion rupees, which is more than 50% of the 6.73 trillion rupee worth of approvals — a 10-year high — in the financial year ended March 2026, Citi said in a report on Tuesday.
While New Delhi has said it plans to procure 82% of the defense equipment from local industries, foreign companies are likely to play a key role in providing technology crucial for military modernization.
Foreign partnerships remain important for technologies that India does not yet produce independently, Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo, told CNBC. India relies on imported technologies for specialized components such as aircraft engines, propulsion systems, sensors and electronic subsystems, he explained.
"American, Israeli, and Russian defense manufacturers are likely to find substantial opportunities in India's expanding defense market," through joint ventures, co-production and technology partnerships with Indian companies, Chaturvedi said.
India was the world's second-largest importer of major arms in 2021–25 with an 8.2% share of total global imports, even as its reliance on overseas suppliers dropped by 4% during the same time due to growing local design and production abilities, according to SIPRI.
New Delhi is also the world's fifth-largest military spender, with $92 billion, but this is less than 30% of Chinese military expenditure and around a 10th of America's, Wezeman of SIPRI pointed out.
India faces some practical challenges in matching China's scale of military modernization, but the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have shown that mass-produced systems like drones can address asymmetry, Collin Koh Swee Lean, a senior fellow at Singapore's Nanyang Technological University, said.

articles.title_orig: US and Japan, long alarmed by China's aggression, agree to establish missile-production facility
articles.title_zh: US and Japan, long alarmed by China's aggression, agree to establish missile-production facility
articles.content_orig:
US military says the restrictions on the electric vehicles at Kadena airbase also apply to delivery drivers and taxis
One of America’s biggest overseas military bases has banned vehicles made by the Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD over security concerns, the US military in Japan said on Tuesday.
The ban, which went into effect this week at Kadena airbase on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa , has fueled speculation that similar measures could be taken at other US military facilities as part of Washington’s crackdown on Chinese technology it suspects of being used to collect sensitive information.
“These vehicles present an unacceptable and unmitigable risk to our personnel and our mission,” Lieut Col Alli Stormer, a spokesperson for the US air force 18th Wing at Kadena, said in a statement.
The restrictions apply to all BYD vehicles, including privately owned cars, taxis and delivery vehicles, reports said, adding that security personnel stationed at the base’s gates had been instructed to block BYD vehicles and instruct drivers to turn around.
Kadena, the biggest US air force base east Asia, would be directly involved in responding to a crisis involving China , Russia or North Korea .
Its inventory includes the powerful Typhon missile system, which is said to be capable of firing Tomahawk missiles as far as 1,600km, putting parts of China and Russia within striking distance. Kadena also hosts fighter planes and aircraft used for mid-air refuelling, surveillance and reconnaissance, according to its website.
The move comes amid concerns of potential information leaks via vehicle-mounted technologies such as cameras, sensors and GPS devices, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency said.
American military officials have not identified a specific threat, but the ban is part of wider measures taken by the US and other western countries to restrict Chinese smart technology in vehicles, mobile phones and other devices they fear could be used to “spy” on their owners.
In June the Pentagon added BYD to a list of 188 Chinese firms it believes have ties to the country’s military, drawing a protest from Beijing. The blacklist also includes the automaker Nio, e-commerce firm Alibaba and internet company Baidu.
The US defence department banned the sale and use of smartphones from Chinese companies Huawei and ZTE at military bases worldwide in 2018, again citing security concerns.
China has imposed similar restrictions on US-made Tesla vehicles. In 2021, it barred them from some government compounds due to security concerns over ⁠cameras installed on the vehicles. Beijing removed that restriction in 2024 after Tesla won an endorsement from the country’s top auto industry association.
BYD, which has not immediately responded publicly to the Kadena ban, overtook Tesla as the world’s biggest seller of battery-electric vehicles in 2025.
It is now expanding overseas, including in the world’s fourth-biggest auto market, Japan , where in July it launched its Racco electric minicar in the hope that the small, cost-efficient vehicle would carve out a place in a market dominated by domestic brands.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Alphabet, Microsoft Earnings in Focus; Fed Holds Rates — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Alphabet, Microsoft Earnings in Focus; Fed Holds Rates — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business.
Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus:
Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business.
The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported  $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion.
With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue.
For Azure, Hood said she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus.
"We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," the company's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts.
Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue.
Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues.
"In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said. The delays have to do with GPU-as-a-service providers, she said.
Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time.
Microsoft will continue to generate free cash flow through the 2027 fiscal year, but the company will access additional sources of funding when it's attractive to do so, Hood said.
"We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our rates ratings are, and sort of we haven't been able to — we haven't yet, I would say, tapped that," she said. "And then, of course, there's other options."
Microsoft's net income increased to $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million loss on its investment in OpenAI.
For the first time, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter, despite the delays from third-party providers.
Analysts polled by StreetAccount expected $32.32 billion. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%.
Microsoft reported results under two operating segments — Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.  For the past 11 years, the company had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses.
In Agents and Infra, revenue rose almost 25% to $76.8 billion, more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services.
The number of people using the Microsoft 365 Copilot AI assistant is up 50% from last quarter, CEO Satya Nadella said on the call. The company did not disclose the number of paid seats. The recently announced high-end Microsoft 365 E7 productivity bundle now has millions of seats, Hood said.
Revenue in the Devices and Consumer business slipped 3% to $15.48 billion, beating the StreetAccount consensus of $15.05 billion. The unit includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers.
Sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%, as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. The company pointed to the end of support for Windows 10 last year and weak PC demand.
As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period.
During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities.

articles.title_orig: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.title_zh: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.content_orig:
The Villa Vie Odyssey was more than 750 days into its voyage around the world when it came to a stop in Cambodia
A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia.
The US-based operator of the Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements".
It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world".
Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship's operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 (Â£6,000) from $1,800.
Villa Vie Residences said it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port". But those measures turned out to be insufficient to "offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs".
"Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," it said.
The company would spend the next 60 days on "restructuring and recapitalisation", though "no outcome is assured", it said.
There were reportedly around 200 passengers on board when they were ordered to disembark in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, a once sleepy beach town that has gained global notoriety in recent years as a hub for Chinese casinos and scam centres.
The Villa Vie Odyssey's voyage was expected to span 3.5 years and cover nearly 150 countries, according to its website.
Its departure had faced delays as the ship underwent repairs, leaving passengers stranded in Belfast for months and costing the company millions of pounds.
The ship was more than 750 days into its circumnavigation before announcing its suspension of its journey on Tuesday - which means its passengers would now be stranded in Cambodia.
Passengers Lanette Canen and Johan Bodin told the BBC they were informed by Villa Vie Residences' chief executive at 6am on Tuesday that they had to leave by 2pm on the same day.
The couple said passengers had known for some time about the company's financial difficulties. A potential investor had previously come onboard the ship to do due dilligence, but in the end it did not work out.
"Even then, we were still hoping a miracle investor would come through," they said. "Although there were signs that this would happen, we still felt disbelief when it became real. We were heartbroken. It felt like our dream had been crushed."
"There have been a lot of hugs and tears as residents support one another and process what has happened."
Another passenger Holly Hennessey said that the ship's passengers had earlier been asked to consider paying a fuel surcharge as global prices soared, and that their itinerary had been "severely curtailed".
Some people decided to disembark and travel on land, she said.
"It was not on my bingo card of places where I'd be spending a lot of time," Hennessey told the BBC from Cambodia.
"We're all in different hotels; there are a number of shipmates in the hotel that I'm in. We're just waiting."
Canen and Bodin said the location in Cambodia was "a difficult place to disembark" because of the distance to a major international airport.
Cruise passenger Holly Hennessey and her cat, Captain, have now found themselves in Cambodia
During their time onboard the Villa Vie Odyssey, passengers had access to several bars and restaurants, a pool deck and a pickleball court, according to its website.
Permanent residencies in its cabins ranged from $120,000 to $440,000. Those cabins were also available for rent from $3,500 a month.
Last year, the company launched a lifetime residence programme for people to spend their retirement years at sea.
In 2024, days after US President Donald Trump won his second term, Villa Vie Residences announced a four-year "Skip Forward" package.
Its CEO told Fox Business at the time that it was the "perfect product for those who said they'd leave the country if 'XYZ' wins the election".
For Canen and Bodin the experience was "worth it", despite the fact it was shorter than expected.
"We loved our two years on Odysseyâthe adventures, the places we visited and the friends we made along the way."
Many of the passengers have already made plans to "settle together off the ship, so those friendships and that sense of community are continuing on land", they said.
The couple plans to spend a few days in Sihanoukville, before travelling to different parts of South East Asia while they "figure out our next chapter".
But others, like Hennessey, have decided to stick around in Cambodia in the hopes that the Odyssey will set sail again soon.
"Until they say we are done - done done - I am not giving up. I could never duplicate this lifestyle. The idea of going home? It would be so trite," she said.
"Cambodia's not the worst place to hang out."
Additional reporting by Thanya Doksone.

articles.title_orig: One passport isn’t enough for some wealthy Chinese. Here’s where they’re looking next
articles.title_zh: One passport isn’t enough for some wealthy Chinese. Here’s where they’re looking next
articles.content_orig:
For some wealthy Chinese, securing a foreign passport is becoming the ultimate trade-off: giving up their Chinese citizenship.
Wealth advisors say a growing number of affluent Chinese are considering renouncing their nationality as Beijing intensifies scrutiny of offshore wealth, with concerns over taxes, geopolitical uncertainty and greater international mobility driving their interest in alternative passports.
China does not recognize dual nationality, meaning Chinese nationals seeking to acquire foreign citizenship must renounce their passports.
"We have had some clients who are willing to give up their Chinese citizenship to hold multiple passports," said Armand Arton, CEO of immigration migration consultancy Arton Capital, who added that the choice of passports depends on their lifestyle and business needs.
Meanwhile, Ryan Lin, director at Singapore-based legal firm Bayfront Law, said he has seen an increase in wealthy Chinese considering renouncing their nationality since July.
That month, Beijing introduced new measures targeting offshore trusts, with certain incomes and transactions potentially subject to a 20% tax. The changes have prompted some families to reassess how they hold and transfer assets overseas.
Previously, clients would discuss the possibility of giving up their citizenship. Now, more are expressing concrete intentions to do so, Lin told CNBC.
Manish Tibrewal, co-founder of multi-family office Farro Capital, also reported growing interest in foreign passports.
The wealth advisory firm is helping some Chinese families pursue Caribbean citizenship alongside Singapore permanent residency, with the longer-term possibility of obtaining Singapore citizenship, subject to government approval.
Tibrewal said the number of Chinese families actively exploring alternative citizenship options since July far exceeds those who have completed the process last year.
Inquiries from Chinese clients have risen 33% since July, investment migration firm Savory & Partners said, while Global Citizen Solutions reported an increase of nearly 40% compared with the same period last year.
Both firms specialize in investment migration, which helps wealthy individuals obtain foreign residency or citizenship, often through qualifying investments in their destination countries.
Renouncing Chinese citizenship does not automatically erase existing tax liabilities though.
Individuals could remain liable for taxes on historical gains, depending on how their wealth was structured, even after giving up their nationality, but a genuine change in citizenship and residency could affect future obligations, experts said.
For many wealthy Chinese, relinquishing their nationality remains a significant sacrifice, particularly for those whose businesses and fortunes are tied to the mainland.
Lin said those most willing to take that step generally have few remaining business links to China, with much of their wealth and operations already based offshore.
So where are they looking to move?
For wealthy Chinese seeking an alternative passport rather than merely overseas residency, the Caribbean has emerged as a popular choice.
Countries such as Antigua and Barbuda offer citizenship-by-investment programs that allow eligible applicants to obtain nationality through qualifying investments or contributions.
Tibrewal said Caribbean citizenship can potentially be secured within six months, making it considerably faster than pathways in Europe or the United States, where residency requirements often precede naturalization.
Arton said the appeal is less about permanently relocating and more about greater flexibility to travel and establish an international base.
Global Citizen Solutions said the Caribbean recorded the strongest growth in Chinese inquiries among the destinations it tracked this year.
European countries are also attracting interest, although many offer residency pathways rather than immediate citizenship.
"For Chinese HNWIs who are not willing to give up their citizenship, a portfolio of residencies or long-term visas is a more appealing option," Arton said.
Portugal remains popular through its golden visa program, which offers residency through qualifying investments and a potential longer-term route to citizenship.
Arton also added that Italy is attracting wealthy families through its favorable tax arrangements for qualifying new residents, international schools and financial services infrastructure.
Hungary is another emerging destination, offering long-term residency through qualifying investments starting at 250,000 euros ($290,000).
“Hungary is the one that surprises people,” according to Global Citizen Solutions. “As the larger European golden visa routes have closed or become more expensive, Hungary offers residency in the Schengen area through a regulated fund investment.”
Singapore remains attractive to wealthy Chinese because of its political stability, established wealth management industry, international schools and proximity to mainland China.
Some families are pursuing Singapore permanent residency as part of longer-term citizenship plans, although naturalization is neither automatic nor guaranteed.
Tibrewal said his firm was assisting some clients with plans involving Caribbean citizenship and Singapore residency, with Singapore citizenship a possible longer-term objective.
Australia is another popular option, particularly for families prioritizing education and quality of life.
Malaysia is also gaining attention, especially Kuala Lumpur and Penang, where lower living costs, Chinese-speaking communities and international schools appeal to families, said the migration consultancies.
"We also see interest beyond the obvious hubs in Asia, including Penang and Thailand's long-term resident visa, from families who value lifestyle and lower costs," said Global Citizen Solutions.
Meanwhile, Argentina and parts of Eastern Europe are emerging as alternative destinations for those seeking to diversify their international residency options.
Arton Capital identified Argentina as a market worth watching, while Savory & Partners highlighted growing interest in Serbia, North Macedonia and Bulgaria.
Advisors caution that interest in overseas citizenship does not necessarily translate into completed renunciations or physical relocations.
"It's important to recognize that exploring overseas residency, building a passport portfolio, and relocating an entire family are very different decisions," Arton said.

articles.title_orig: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years
articles.title_zh: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years
articles.content_orig:
The Song dynasty sculptures were given to the National Gallery of Australia in the 1990s, a time when art theft was rife in China
Australia has returned two stone sculptures to China after more than 30 years abroad.
The statues, showing the heads of a military official and civil servant, had been given to the National Gallery of Australia in Canberra by a private collector and date back to the Northern Song dynasty (960–1127).
China’s National Cultural Heritage Administration received the heads on Wednesday, according to the state broadcaster CCTV.

articles.title_orig: Marvell Is Said to Near Deal for Lumentum In AI-Related Megadeal
articles.title_zh: Marvell Is Said to Near Deal for Lumentum In AI-Related Megadeal
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
A final deal hasn't been reached, and details could change, the report said.
After Wednesday's market close, Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, while Marvell is valued near $221 billion.
A potential combination would give Marvell access to scarce, high-performance optical components which can help ease bottlenecks in AI clusters.
Shares of Lumentum Holdings Inc (LITE) soared 10% after hours on Wednesday following a report that Marvell Technology is in talks to buy it in a potential megadeal.
A deal between Marvell and the data center optics maker could be announced as soon as next week, Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter. A final deal hasn't been reached, and details could change, the report said.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
After Wednesday's market close, Lumentum has a market value of about $83 billion, while Marvell is valued near $221 billion. Shares of MRVL tumbled 8% following the report.
Marvell is a fabless semiconductor designer focused on data-infrastructure solutions, while Lumentum makes optical and photonic products such as lasers, optical components, and networking systems used in cloud and AI data centers. Lumentum's indium-phosphide technology is particularly in high demand; CEO Michael Hurlston has previously said that the company is essentially sold out of certain products into 2029 and is under-shipping demand by substantial margins due to the fast-paced nature of AI data center buildouts.
Marvell, too, is strengthening its position in the AI space, recently inking a partnership with Google on custom chips. The company also completed acquiring Celestial AI, specialized in photonic interconnect technology to remove data bottlenecks in AI data centers, earlier this year.
A potential combination would give Marvell access to scarce, high-performance optical components which can help ease bottlenecks in AI clusters by replacing copper interconnects which are more limited in capacity.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around LITE stock jumped from bearish to bullish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from 'normal' to 'high' levels.
Meanwhile, sentiment around MRVL stayed at 'bearish' levels, accompanied by 'normal' retail chatter.
A Stocktwits user voiced optimism for the deal, highlighting that Lumentum is also a successful company and opined that MRVL bears are misjudging the potential deal.
Another user opined that investors should short Marvell and buy Lumentum if the deal materializes.
While LITE stock has gained 148% year-to-date, MRVL has added about 196%.

articles.title_orig: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme
articles.title_zh: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.
Apple has officially entered the touchscreen MacBook Pro era, and apparently, it wants to drain your wallet while it’s at it.
The new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, which is already a hefty price tag in this economy. But if you want the absolute top-of-the-line model with every possible upgrade, prepare to cough up around $14,549.
As MacRumors first reported, Apple’s configurator prices the fully loaded 14-inch model at $14,249 and the 16-inch version at $14,549. Both come equipped with Apple’s top-tier M5 Max chip, featuring an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU.
You can blame the ongoing memory shortage and AI’s seemingly endless appetite for hardware for some of the pricing pressure. Moving to a 4TB SSD costs an additional $1,000, while upgrading to 8TB adds $3,000. Want the new 16TB option? That’ll set you back another $7,000.
Another $2,000 gets you 128GB of memory, while nano-texture glass adds $150.
For some perspective, the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The new model raises that ceiling by a whopping $4,400.
Absurd prices aside, the launch marks a significant shift for Apple, nearly a decade after it first experimented with the Touch Bar . The company eventually abandoned that feature, but now it’s ready to embrace a touchscreen MacBook Pro.
Preorders open October 30, with availability beginning November 6.

articles.title_orig: What Robinhood's CFO found interesting about Anthropic's IPO prospectus
articles.title_zh: What Robinhood's CFO found interesting about Anthropic's IPO prospectus
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Seemingly, everyone is digging into Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus this week, even other C-suite execs like Robinhood ( HOOD ) CFO Shiv Verma.
"I have gone through it. The growth rates are pretty incredible, … up 1,300% year over year, I can't recall seeing another company doing that well," Verma said on Yahoo Finance about what caught his attention from the prospectus.
"The other thing I thought was interesting is they were showing what percentage of their customers are in different buckets," Verma added. "And so if you spend more than $10 million a year, you're a top 250 customer. I thought that was a pretty interesting stat, as I thought it'd be a little bit larger, but it just goes to show you how big their future TAM [total addressable market] is."
Verma has no choice but to read every single page of the S-1 for at least two reasons.
For one, Verma runs point on Robinhood Ventures.
It's a concentrated investment portfolio heavily anchored in premier AI and data infrastructure giants, including OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), Databricks ( DATB.PVT ), the AI-hiring platform Mercor, and the coding assistant Cognition. So how Anthropic is received by investors could greatly impact the valuations of the companies in the portfolio and, by extension, the overall value of Robinhood.
Secondly, there will likely be a lot of interest from Robinhood's retail investor base, enthralled with all things AI, in trading Anthropic shares and also to use the hotly anticipated debut to scale in and out of other AI names.
As it stands, the S-1 has been generally well received by markets.
Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed. The filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, a strong signal of aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.
On an adjusted basis, Anthropic posted $1.62 billion in operating income through the first six months of 2026 compared to a loss of $1.85 billion last year.
The company is winning praise for its strong top-line growth rates and more than $131 billion in cash on hand.
Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.
Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft's cloud growth, cash flow offer respite from AI spending fears
articles.title_zh: Microsoft's cloud growth, cash flow offer respite from AI spending fears
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Two tech behemoths -- Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) -- reported earnings today. Both showed strong cloud growth, but the market is treating them very differently. Microsoft shares popped after hours while Alphabet stock sank. Why?
I think a big part of the answer is how each plans to pay for the massive outlays both have planned.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
Microsoft beat Wall Street's targets with sales up 19%, reaching $92.3 billion. GAAP -- generally accepted accounting principles -- earnings per share (EPS) came in at $4.92. Adjusted EPS was $4.89, above the roughly $4.72 the Street expected. Azure, its cloud platform, grew 48%, reaching $33.17 billion in revenue.
Alphabet's cloud growth was even stronger than Microsoft's: 103% growth for the unit, earning $11.1 billion in operating income on $30.7 billion in sales. Overall, sales jumped 25%, reaching $127.6 billion, slightly missing estimates, while GAAP EPS actually fell from $2.87 to $2.12. Search and YouTube ads also underperformed.
Some of Alphabet's EPS drop can be explained by an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, but even if you remove this -- worth $0.55 per share -- the earnings still came in well below what Wall Street was looking for.
While it's not a great look, I think the real issue the market is reacting to is the company's cash picture. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditures (capex), up from $24.0 billion a year ago. Operating cash flow -- the cash the actual business generated -- was $42.3 billion. That left free cash flow (FCF) -- the money left after paying for its capex investments -- at negative $9.1 billion. That's worse than the negative $5.9 billion the company reported last quarter.
During the quarter, Alphabet raised $28.7 billion through senior unsecured notes and $12.4 billion from selling stock. Long-term debt has grown from $46.5 billion at the end of 2025 to $125.1 billion.
Alphabet said its capex guidance for 2026 holds -- $195 billion to $205 billion -- but said it expects capex in 2027 to "increase significantly."
Microsoft, on the other hand, is still FCF positive, though like Alphabet, that figure is moving in the wrong direction. The company reported FCF of $18.63 billion, down 27% year over year, after $39.37 billion in cash capital spending. Its broader capex figure, which includes finance leases, was $45.2 billion.
CFO Amy Hood said on July's earnings call that the company expects to stay free-cash-flow positive for its current fiscal year, though capex is expected to expand. On that call, she also said demand for its cloud services was running ahead of supply.
Microsoft at this point has a much healthier cushion in its quarterly cash flow -- more room to keep spending while it waits for those investments to pay off. Alphabet is increasingly asking lenders and shareholders to help cover the bill.
Obviously, the growth is hard to argue with, but I still think the jury is out on whether this bet will pay off for both companies. Costs are climbing, and I'm concerned the math won't pencil out long term.

articles.title_orig: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
articles.title_zh: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
articles.content_orig:
Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides. A new policy will make it easier for small compounding pharmacies to make them. Heather Diehl/Getty Images hide caption
Unproven but popular peptides touted for wellness have been available on the gray market, despite an official ban. Now, the Department of Health and Human Services is looking to bring them out of the shadows.
HHS said in a new policy that it will exercise enforcement discretion for a half dozen peptides, essentially looking the other way when they're made by small compounding pharmacies.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a vocal supporter of peptides , saying he has used some of them himself.
Peptides are strings of amino acids, shorter than proteins, that can exert powerful effects in the body. Some occur naturally and others are synthetic variations. Wellness influencers and some clinicians have promoted unproven peptides for a wide range of uses, though the evidence for their safety and effectiveness is sparse.
So even though these peptides have not been through the Food and Drug Administration's rigorous drug review and approval process, they could become easier to get. But the policy's focus on smaller producers may mean that pharmacists will have a tough time meeting demand.
In July, a panel of advisers to the FDA voted in favor of expanded access to six peptides through compounding pharmacies. However, at the same meeting the FDA's own scientists recommended against unwinding the existing restrictions on them.
The new policy says compounding is a safer alternative to illicit "research-use-only" peptides that are available online. They're often sourced from sketchy suppliers overseas.
The peptides, and some of their unproven uses, are:
Joshua Fritzler, the president of Olympia and Wesley Pharmaceuticals in central Florida, says people have been asking about these peptides for years. But because they were illegal to compound, his company didn't make them.
The new policy doesn't change their legal status, but it does create a path for small compounders, called 503A compounding pharmacies. It doesn't apply to the larger ones, called 503Bs, that are outsourcing facilities producing higher volumes of medicines.
So at Fritzler's company, only its smaller compounding facility will be able to make the peptides – and only in small quantities, he says.
And that has implications for consumers.
"We won't be able to meet demand," he says, explaining that Olympia will likely only compound one of the six peptides and needs to get its facility ready first. "I don't think all the [503]As in the country could meet the demand."
The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding's CEO Scott Brunner wrote in a statement that his group is pleased with the administration's decision to allow the peptides to be compounded because it offers a "more accountable alternative" for patients seeking gray market peptides.
"It also brings patients into a system where pharmacy standards, regulatory oversight, and serious adverse event reporting apply," he says.
Brunner warned, however, that it may take some time for compounding pharmacies to begin dispensing these products to patients. That's because ingredient suppliers need to make sure their active ingredients meet the policy's requirements — and pharmacies need to verify that, too.
Several consumer advocacy groups say the policy puts patients at risk, however. The nonprofit Public Citizen noted that Kennedy seems to have acted unilaterally rather than through the typical rulemaking process.
"By allowing unproven and potentially unsafe peptides to be manufactured, marketed and prescribed without concern about potential federal enforcement actions, Kennedy has undermined the FDA and threatened public health," Dr. Robert Steinbrook, Health Research Group Director at Public Citizen wrote in a statement. "All peptide substances should go through the standard FDA approval process for new drugs. The HHS Secretary should support, not sabotage, needed FDA enforcement actions to protect consumers."
Steinbrook advised clinicians to talk to their patients and tell them about the risk of contamination and other adverse effects.
The Partnership for Safe Medicines, which includes various pharmacy and pharmacist organizations around the country, filed a citizen petition last week, urging the FDA to ignore the recommendation from its advisory committee in July to allow compounding pharmacies to make the six peptides.
"Today's decision leaves Americans in a grey area as to whether peptides are safe or not, even though the FDA's own scientists recommended against voting in favor of these substances due to concerns with evidence," its executive director Shabbir Safda wrote in a statement.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
articles.content_orig:
Isabel Kershner Johnatan Reiss Aaron Boxerman Qasim Nauman and Leo Sands
Israel’s political leaders were bracing for weeks of negotiations over a new government, as initial results on Wednesday showed no clear winner in a tightly fought election that many have described as a make-or-break moment for the country.
By Wednesday evening in Israel, election officials had counted about 90 percent of the ballots. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hard-line bloc of parties held a modest lead in seats over the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, but it appears that neither coalition will win the 61 seats needed to secure a straightforward majority in the Knesset, Israel’s Parliament.
That means both leaders would need to find support from outside their coalitions to form a government. Two Arab parties were on track to win as many as 19 seats, a strong showing that potentially gives them an important role in the negotiations, even though most Jewish parties were not eager to enter an alliance with them.
Some of Mr. Netanyahu’s allies have floated the idea that he could join Mr. Eisenkot and other centrists to form a broad unity government to stay in power. For Mr. Netanyahu, who will remain a caretaker prime minister until a government is formed, that would be a comfortable scenario.
Mr. Eisenkot faces a dilemma. He has denounced Mr. Netanyahu as unfit to lead Israel, but he has also objected to partnering with Arab parties in a potential coalition. On Wednesday, Mr. Eisenkot did not explicitly mention the Arab parties but said he was focused on forming a government that was both Zionist and committed to universal military conscription, a message that rules out alliances with both Arab and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.
The Joint List, an alliance of Arab parties that has emerged as a potential kingmaker according to preliminary results, said it would “do everything in its power” to remove Mr. Netanyahu from office. That could signal a willingness to back Mr. Eisenkot’s bid to form an anti-Netanyahu coalition, even if its lawmakers have not been invited to join it.
The final tally of votes is not expected to be finished before Thursday evening. Lengthy negotiations are likely to follow as political parties try to assemble a governing majority. If those talks fail, the country could head to a second round of elections — a scenario that has played out before.
Here’s what else we are covering:
Vote count: The nearly 90 percent of votes counted indicate that Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition will receive about 54 seats, Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc will get roughly 49, and the Arab parties could reach as many as 19. But the numbers could still shift.
Parliamentary control: Even if no government is formed, the Israeli Parliament will open on Nov. 10, and Mr. Netanyahu’s opponents could be well-placed to take control of the legislative process. Read more ›
Herzog’s role: President Isaac Herzog of Israel holds a largely ceremonial position, except after national elections, when it falls to him to select who gets the first crack at forming a new government. Read more ›
What Israelis think: The day after Israel’s election, almost everyone in the country was asking the same question: What now? The Times spoke to people from across the political spectrum to get a sense of their hopes and fears. Read more ›
For decades, Israel’s Arab parties have been relegated to the margins of Israeli political life, often sitting on the sidelines while Jewish parties assembled a governing coalition in Parliament and picked a prime minister.
Heading into Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned his supporters that the Arabs were “trying to steal the election,” though electoral officials said there were no reports of widespread irregularities. He repeatedly invoked the specter of Arab voters to galvanize his right-wing base, vowing to keep them out of power.
Mr. Netanyahu’s leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, largely declined to answer whether he would partner with Arab parties if necessary to topple the Netanyahu government, though he said none met his conditions as potential allies.
But record turnout on Tuesday by supporters of the Arab parties looks to deliver them their largest vote totals in generations, possibly since Israel’s establishment 78 years ago.
Now, the Arab minority represents a political reality that cannot be ignored.
Turnout in the Arab community, which represents about 20 percent of Israeli citizens, appears to have translated into a stunning windfall of parliamentary seats — potentially as many as 19 combined between the two leading parties, Raam and the Joint List alliance. The Arab parties have 10 seats in the outgoing Parliament.
Israel’s future could turn in part on whether Mr. Eisenkot decides to take the political risks of partnering with them. Without their support, Mr. Eisenkot and his alliance will almost certainly fall short of the 61-seat majority required in the 120-seat Parliament to form a new government and end Mr. Netanyahu’s hold on power. Mr. Netanyahu’s alliance also looks to fall short of 61 seats.
Many Israeli Jews have long objected to building a governing coalition that relies on Arab party backing for a majority. Some say a Jewish state should be ruled exclusively by Jews. Some cite national security reasons, questioning whether Arab leaders who see themselves as part of the wider Palestinian people can be entrusted with crucial matters of state.
Those objections became even more acute after the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel and the subsequent rightward shift in Israeli politics. Both Raam and some members of the Joint List condemned the assault, although they have also been highly critical of how Israel has conducted its war against Hamas in Gaza.
The Arab parties for many years were themselves reluctant to join governments that oversaw the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza. And turnout among Arab Israelis has traditionally been lower than Jewish turnout, reflecting doubts about their ability to influence national decision-making.
Raam, a socially conservative party with roots in Islamist politics, has achieved some acceptance in Israel’s mainstream by putting less emphasis on the cause of Palestinian statehood. But the Joint List, an alliance of three smaller parties that includes a joint Jewish-Arab leftist faction and a Palestinian nationalist faction, is seen as more antagonistic toward Zionism.
Initial election results show that the Joint List will be the significantly larger of the two in Parliament.
“Netanyahu knows that without the Arab parties, there’s no majority to unseat him. That’s why he incites against us,” said Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Joint List alliance in an interview. “The opposition should reject that incitement.”
He added: “The ball is now in Eisenkot’s court. Whoever wants to remove Netanyahu and change his policies — we are ready to cooperate to topple his government.”
Political analysts say the Joint List would be more likely to support Eisenkot from outside the governing coalition, for instance by agreeing to block any no-confidence votes. There is some precedent for this: In the 1990s, then Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin relied on Arab lawmakers to prevent the collapse of his own minority government.
Arab citizens, some of whom view themselves as both Israeli and Palestinian, experience a tension that can cut to the heart of daily life. Unlike Palestinians in the West Bank — who live under Israeli military rule — Arab Israelis can vote, and some have held high office, including on the country’s Supreme Court.
But they largely live in separate cities and towns from Jewish Israelis and retain tight familial and historical bonds with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. Many view themselves as second-class citizens in the Jewish state, saying they face discrimination in housing as well as neglect in receiving public services.

articles.title_orig: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.title_zh: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.content_orig:
The horrific crash south of Madrid was caused by human error after a computer system failure, officials say
• Deadly rail crash: Scores of people have been killed and about 100 injured after a high-speed train collided with a stationary train south of Madrid. Spain’s transport minister called it “inexplicable” that a train was allowed to continue its journey despite a red signal being in place.
• ‘People were hurled into the air ’: Several witnesses told CNN about the chaotic moment when passengers were thrown airborne during the collision. Rescue operations are still ongoing and the high-speed line linking Madrid with Andalusia remains suspended.
• Third train crash this year: This is the third rail disaster in Spain in 2026. In January, two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz , in southern Spain’s Córdoba province, killing more than 40 people. A commuter train near Barcelona derailed days later.
• Lee nuestra cobertura en español
Our live coverage has ended. Read more about the deadly train crash here .
At least 68 people were killed and about 100 were injured after a high-speed train smashed into a stationary train in Spain on Wednesday.
Crews are now working with flood lights to search for anyone else trapped in the wreckage as investigators try to figure out what led to the tragedy.
What we know : A computer system failure led to an issue with the safety system along a 63-kilometer (40-mile) stretch of track between Madrid and Seville causing all trains in the area to be stopped automatically, said Óscar Puente, the country’s transport minister.
Puente said Adif, the state-owned company that manages Spain’s railways, then took manual command of the system and allowed the high-speed Renfe train to continue southbound toward Seville despite a red light. That train later collided with the stationary Iryo train.
Response: More than 500 emergency personnel have been deployed to the site, the Spanish Interior Ministry said. The Civil Guard said investigators are using drones to create a 3D reconstruction of the area and determine the accident’s possible causes.
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said authorities are working hard to identify the cause of the crash and vowed that any negligence, if identified, will be addressed with “utmost firmness.” This is the third rail incident in Spain this year.
CNN’s Billy Stockwell, Michael Rios, Pau Mosquera and Duarte Mendonca, Jennifer Hansler, Sophie Tanno and Sol Amaya contributed reporting to this post.
Police were seen clashing with protesters and far right groups in the Spanish capital Madrid on Wednesday night as crowds demanded the resignation of Spanish government officials following a deadly train crash that left at least 68 dead.
Around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry, with some throwing bottles and flares at police, Reuters reported. Video showed police deploying tear gas in an attempt disperse the large group gathered.
Protesters held signs saying “Leave!” next to a picture of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, while others held signs saying “Criminals” and “Corruption kills.” Sanchez’s socialist PSOE party has suffered a series of setbacks and corruption scandals this year involving close associates that have tarnished its reputation.
Spanish trade union CSIF is demanding the resignation of Óscar Puente, the country’s transport minister, after he said an “inexplicable” erroneous order from a train controller resulted in Wednesday’s deadly crash .
While discussing the circumstances of the collision, Puente said a computer system failure led to an issue with the safety system along a 63-kilometer (40-mile) stretch of track causing all trains in the area to be stopped automatically.
Puente said Adif, the state-owned company that manages Spain’s railways, then took manual command of the system and a decision was made to allow the high-speed Renfe train to continue southbound toward Seville despite a red light. That train later collided with the stationary Iryo train.
CSIF, an independent trade union and civil servants’ association, accused Puente of using a “hardworking person” as a scapegoat instead of “assuming his responsibilities.” The trade union also said it had warned in September of “excess hours in Adif’s working days.”
CNN has approached Spain’s transport ministry for comment.
CNN’s Lauren Kent contributed reporting.
Renfe, Spain’s state-owned national railway operator, announced it has suspended service Thursday between Madrid and the Andalusia region.
One of Renfe’s trains was involved in a deadly collision earlier today, which killed at least 68 people. The Renfe train plowed into a stationary train operated by the private company Iryo, at a time when all train traffic in the area was disrupted due to a problem with the LZB train management safety system.
The collision occurred on the route between Madrid and Seville and an alternative transportation plan will be provided on Friday, Renfe said.
The service suspension also applies to trains coming from Barcelona and Valencia to Seville and Malaga, Renfe said in a post on X .
Some of cars derailed and officials are still searching for anyone trapped in the rubble.
Ana has been searching for her husband, Pepe, all day. But so far, no luck.
She raced to Madrid as soon as she heard about Wednesday’s deadly train collision in the Spanish province of Toledo, she told Reuters. Pepe was traveling on the high-speed Renfe train that crashed into the stationary Ilyo train while heading from Madrid to Seville.
Ana, who only provided her first name, told Reuters that Pepe’s name was not on the list of victims who have been identified.
Local police did however find Ana’s dog, who had been traveling with Pepe.
“Poor thing, I think he’s had a bad time,” she told Reuters, speaking from a school in Urda – the town closest to the site of the train crash – where relatives have been advised to wait.
Renfe, a state-owned railway company, said it had opened a special phone line for families of victims, Reuters reported.
In the days ahead, investigators in Spain will continue to gather details to understand what exactly led to the deadly train collision that killed at least 68 people, said Janos Rozsa, a railway accident investigator and safety specialist.
Spain’s transport minister said the was crash caused by human error after a computer system failure, but Rozsa said “accidents rarely have a single cause.”
Incidents like this “usually result from a combination of different contributing factors that are present at the same time,” he told CNN’s Isa Soares.
Officials will use things like surveillance cameras and data recorders on the trains and on the signaling system to piece together how the trains were moving and how they ended up on the same piece of track.
While human error may be one part of the what caused the crash, it will also be important for investigators to fully understand “the circumstances in which people were working and how the overall system was designed to keep these trains apart.”
While this is the third rail disaster in Spain this year, Rozsa said it is too early to draw any conclusions if the incidents had any common threads.
Scores of people were killed after two trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, in a crash that authorities say was caused by both computer system failure and apparent human error.

At that point, the state-owned company that manages Spain’s railways, ADIF, took manual command of the system and a decision was made to allow the high-speed Renfe train to continue southbound along the tracks despite a red light.

articles.title_orig: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
articles.title_zh: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
articles.content_orig:
An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German wildlife park.
She was inside an enclosure at the Johannismühle park in Brandenburg, south of Berlin, with a staff member and two other children when the attack happened, police said.
They said in a statement that the "precise circumstances of the incident are the subject of an ongoing police investigation".
The girl was taken to hospital by helicopter after the incident on Wednesday. No one else was injured.
The park, in the town of Baruth/Mark, has been closed temporarily and is set to reopen on 2 November, according to its website, which did not give further details.
The park keeps grey and arctic wolves, along with other animals including the brown bear and lynx.
The girl was injured by at least one animal and suffered head injuries, according to German newspaper Bild.
It reported that the incident happened before the park opened at 10:00 local time (09:00 GMT) and that the girl could have been taking part in a special visit.
Johannismühle offers small group tours to allow visitors to spend time with some animals, with its site mentioning feeding wolves or petting a llama.
The incident comes after a number of other animal attacks at zoos and wildlife parks in Europe.
A keeper at a Dutch zoo died this week after being mauled by a leopard, and a man was killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park earlier this month.

articles.title_orig: King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
articles.title_zh: King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
articles.content_orig:
The King shook off royal formality and replaced it with some dance moves on the second day of his nine-day visit to the Caribbean.
Armed with a pair of maracas in the colours of the flag of the Bahamas, Charles joined a Junkanoo - a cultural event and carnival designed to celebrate island life.
Amidst the feathered headdresses and brightly coloured costumes in the afternoon Caribbean heat, the King, dressed in a suit and sunglasses, joined dancers at the front of parade to cheers from the crowd.
It was a lighter mood coming after the King's arrival on Tuesday where he delivered a speech acknowledging the pain of the slave trade, describing "the suffering of the past".
Speaking at an event in the Bahamas celebrating local youth on Tuesday, the King said the country's culture was "born out of darkness", and it was "only right" to acknowledge historic injustices.
Charles began the second day of his trip by paying his respects to fallen members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force (RBDF).
The King, wearing a set of medals and sunglasses, spoke with servicemen and women before he laid a wreath at the Flamingo Monument, which commemorates four RBDF Marines killed when Cuban MiG fighter aircraft sunk HMBS Flamingo in May 1980.
Later, on a visit to the Bahamas Boxing Academy, the King found young fighters and the head coach wearing an image of himself emblazoned on club t-shirts showing the King complete with a crown, gloves and a boxing belt.
"He loved it, he loved it," said Jermaine Gibson, president of a neighbouring boxing club who wore one of the t-shirts. "He said it was really good and we gave him one of his own."
The King watched two young fighters sparring in the ring at the academy which trains boys and girls from the age of eight to 18 years old.
"I might see you at a Commonwealth Games," the King told a group of children at the boxing academy.
Protecting this region from climate change is a theme of the King's trip and was the focus of his visit to the Bonefish Pond National Park. The site was once a rubbish dump but has been redeveloped and now protects 1,235 acres of mangroves.
The King walked along a new boardwalk through the wetlands to see the conservation work being done to protect this vulnerable, low lying island from climate change.
He met students carrying out field work in the wetland waters asking them about their exams and ambitions to be marine biologists.
"We've so been looking forward to this," said Joanne Smith, President of the Bahamas National Trust Council.
"We want more Bahamians to get involved in our national parks so they can use it to better themselves… we are so pleased to have the King here, this is really significant for us."
Then it was on to the Junkanoo, where the King could be seen dancing alongside attendees dressed in feathered headdresses and bright costumes.
The history of the Junkanoo is not clear but it's believed it emerged out of the slave trade when enslaved men and women were given time off to mark Christmas.
A small protest near the parade was moved on by the police.
The King ended his day with a garden reception at Government House in Nassau where he met Bahamians who have made significant contributions to public life.
In a speech, Dame Cynthia A Pratt, the governor general of the Bahamas who is the King's representative on the island, described her pride at Charles visiting the country for the first time since 1973.
"We trust that your time in our capital will reflect the legendary hospitality of our people," said Dame Cynthia.
"We pray that this royal visit further strengthens the enduring bonds of friendship between the Crown and the Bahamian people."
On Thursday, the Caribbean tour leaves the Bahamas as the King continues his visit in Guyana.
The trip has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda with an emphasis on honouring the past but also looking forward to the ambition and possibility for future generations.
The King will move to Guyana later this week where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity.
He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where he will be joined by Queen Camilla, for the CHOGM and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth.
The biennial summit will bring together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.

articles.title_orig: All 16 D&D World of Warcraft Species Revealed
articles.title_zh: All 16 D&D World of Warcraft Species Revealed
articles.content_orig:
As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.
Over the past twenty years, the World of Warcraft MMORPG has introduced dozens of playable species. Now, many of these unique creatures and cultures are making the leap from the desktop to the tabletop courtesy of the upcoming D&D WoW crossover.
In total there are 16 new D&D WoW species. Five of these (Dwarf, Elf, Goblin, Human and Orc) are adaptations of existing D&D 5.5E species, while 11 of them (Dracthyr, Draenei, Earthen, Forsaken, Gnome, Haranir, Pandaren, Tauren, Troll, Vulpera and Worgen) are completely native to the world of Azeroth and appearing in 5.5E for the first time.
To help make sense of it all, we’ve put together this detailed species guide, which includes a high-level explanation of what the species is all about, along with their key traits within the D&D 5.5E ruleset. One important thing to note is that we have also included notes on Renown , which is an optional rule in the 2024 Dungeon Master’s Guide but is a major part of the new D&D Warcraft supplement. Each species has a base Renown score that determines how you interact with Azeroth’s many factions and offers in-game benefits such as access to magic items, discounts on equipment and new Bastion facilities.
With that in mind, below is a complete breakdown of all 16 species from the D&D WoW supplement. You can check them out for yourself, when the book arrives at your local game store, D&D Beyond and Amazon.
Dracthyr are draconic humanoids (somewhat similar to D&D’s Dragonborn ) who were created thousands of years ago by Neltharion , a god-like demon-dragon and leader of the black dragonflight (one of Azeroth’s five great families of dragons, each of which is tasked with protecting one particular aspect of the world). Neltharion combined the power of dragons with the adaptability of the mortal races to create what he believed would be an army of elite soldiers. Unfortunately, Neltharion was corrupted and driven mad by the Old Gods and became the villainous being known as Deathwing. As a result, his army off dracthyr was sealed away in stasis, sleeping for ten thousand years until they were eventually awakened in the Dragon Isles.
In their natural form, dracthyr are winged, scaled warriors, but can transform into a humanoid form known as a visage. In the World of Warcraft MMORPG, dracthyr are the only species that can play the Evoker class (a mechanic that has carried over into the new D&D supplement). It’s also important to note that within the 5.5E rules, a dracthyr’s creature type is Dragon rather than Humanoid, which does matter when it comes to certain spells, abilities and magic items.
Dracthyr are organized into military divisions called weyrns . When you create a dracthyr, you choose which weyrn you belong to. There are five options in the new D&D WoW supplement:
If you choose the Dark Talons (Horde) or the Obsidian Warders (Alliance), your Renown Score with that faction begins at 3. If you choose any other weyrn, your Renown Score with the Valdrakken Accord (the alliance of dragonflights based in the city of Valdrakken) begins at 3.
As a Dracthyr, you have these special traits.
Draenei are tall, blue-skinned humanoids with hooves, tails and face tendrils, and are one of the few playable species not originally from Azeroth. Instead, they are the descendants of a species known as the Eredar, who once dwelled on the distant world of Argus. When the dark Titan Sargeras offered the Eredar unimaginable power, two of their leaders accepted and became unholy lords of the demonic horde known as the Burning Legion . The third leader, the prophet Velen, foresaw these dark events and fled from Argus with his followers, with the group guided by benevolent beings made of holy energy known as naaru .
The Eredar who travelled with Argus called themselves draenei (which meant “exiled ones” in their language) and spent thousands of years fleeing across the cosmos with the Burning Legion in pursuit. Eventually their dimensional ship, known as the Exodar, crash-landed on Azeroth, where they joined the Alliance.
When you create a Draenei, you choose one of four Eredar Lineages:
If you choose the Draenei or Lightforged lineage, your Renown Score with the Exodar (Alliance) begins at 3. Otherwise, you have no starting Renown Score.
As a Draenei, you have these special traits.
At first glance, Azeroth’s Dwarves will feel familiar to most D&D players and fans of fantasy fiction. They’re stout, stubborn and famous for their mining, stonework, engineering and love of weapons and good ale. Their origin, however, is unique to Warcraft. Dwarves descend from the Earthen, beings of living stone built by the Titans (the godlike cosmic beings who shaped Azeroth). When the Old God Yogg-Saron afflicted the earthen with the “curse of flesh,” many asked to be sealed away in hibernation until a cure could be found. Ages later, they awoke as flesh-and-blood dwarves, journeyed to the snowy mountains of Dun Morogh and carved out the great city of Ironforge.
For more than two thousand years, Ironforge prospered through trade with the human kingdoms to the north. Then, about two centuries before the orcs invaded Azeroth, tensions between its three most powerful clans erupted into a civil conflict called the War of the Three Hammers. The Bronzebeard clan won the war and drove its rivals out of the mountain. Today, those old wounds have largely healed, and Ironforge is governed by the Council of Three Hammers, which includes representatives from all three clans and is considered a founding pillar of the Alliance.
When you create a dwarf, you can choose which clan you hail from. There are four options:
Whichever clan you choose, your Renown Score with Ironforge (Alliance) begins at 3.
You have the Dwarf species traits from the 2024 Player’s Handbook.
As a Dwarf, you have these special traits.
Earthen are beings of living stone created eons ago by the god-like Titans using a great machine called the Forge of Wills and were designed to mine and carve out Azeroth’s caverns. Over time, many earthen fell victim to the “curse of flesh,” which was engineered by the Old God Yogg-Saron. These victims became the ancestors of today’s dwarves. Large populations of stone earthen survived, however, primarily on the continent of Khaz Algar, where a titan device called the Awakening Machine roused them from stasis. After the dwarf king Magni Bronzebeard restored the machine, newly awakened earthen were allowed to choose their own path rather than follow the titans’ ancient instructions, and many have since joined the Alliance or the Horde.
In appearance, earthen resemble stocky dwarves carved from stone and infused with Azerite, the crystallized lifeblood of Azeroth. Crystals jut from their bodies and mineral growths take the place of hair and beards. They don’t need to eat, but consuming certain minerals or precious stones can slightly alter their appearance.
As newly awakened free agents with no long-standing ties to either faction, Earthen have no starting Renown Score.
As an Earthen, you have these special traits.
Every Elf of Azeroth traces their roots to the night elves, who once ruled a world-spanning empire built around a lake of raw magical energy known as the Well of Eternity. Their rulers soon became obsessed with arcane magic, which drew the attention of the Burning Legion . The resulting War of the Ancients ended with the Great Sundering, a cataclysm that shattered Azeroth’s single continent into the landmasses that exist today. Ten thousand years of conflict have since splintered elven society into several distinct peoples, five of which are playable in the new D&D 5.5E supplement:

Rimea shared the discovery on social media, as first found by MondoMega. The following drivers are in a file that relates to the character weight stats:

articles.title_orig: Election polls in New Zealand continue to show no clear outcome
articles.title_zh: Election polls in New Zealand continue to show no clear outcome
articles.content_orig:
RNZ / News / Politics / Election 2026
Link: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/politics_election-2026/2211552%2Fnational-party-mps-feeling-the-pressure-of-party-vote-plunge
Audio player for " Political editor Jo Moir discusses latest RNZ poll " removed for printing
Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/politics_election-2026/2211552%2Fnational-party-mps-feeling-the-pressure-of-party-vote-plunge
Analysis - National is in a fight to save the furniture just nine days out from the polls closing.
The latest RNZ-Reid Research poll has the governing party falling below the 25 percent mark - collecting just 24.8 points as it nears the home stretch to 7 November.
That result is a drop on the 25.9 points it registered in our poll three weeks ago, and even worse than the 25.6 percent National got in the dire 2020 election result.
This poll puts an almost six-point gap between National and Labour, which registered 30.6 percent.
While National is in real danger territory, its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First are sitting on 10.1 and 9.9 respectively, putting the gap between their combined vote and National's at less than five percent.
In a sign the strategic voting phenomenon being pitched by some on the centre-right could be resonating, ACT is up 1.1 - a direct swap with National, which is down by the exact same number.
The strategy is built on the idea that voters on the right give their candidate vote to National and their party vote to ACT or New Zealand First, which has the effect of creating an overhang with National winning more electorate seats than its allocated party vote proportion.
It's a play that has National Party list MPs and those in marginal seats, who are relying on a strong party vote, pulling their hair out as they look at poll after poll with their chances of getting into Parliament diminishing.
Look no further than Paul Goldsmith who has resorted to sending out letters in his electorate asking Epsom voters to "do things differently" and give him the electorate vote as "David Seymour is guaranteed to be re-elected on the ACT Party list".
Adding it would be the "greatest honour" of his career to be the MP for Epsom. Not only that, on RNZ's poll numbers it's the only way he'll be an MP with his list spot of sixth far from safe.
Deputy leader Nicola Willis, senior MP and minister Chris Bishop, and Speaker Gerry Brownlee are in similarily precarious positions and there's two places to point the finger.
Audio player for " Giles Dexter reports in latest RNZ poll results " removed for printing
Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._f0.YIZs2-J2FpwgcBcJJb29s1vXmFAWHLh_p1oUyv-l-RA/politics_election-2026/2211552%2Fnational-party-mps-feeling-the-pressure-of-party-vote-plunge
One is a global trend of major parties' falling support in democracies abroad, and political fragmentation leading to previously minor parties growing in support.
That trend has seen the purple vote - the combined Labour and National vote - drop steadily across the course of the year and down to just 55.4 percent in this poll.
The other contributor to National's woes is the Christopher Luxon-shaped hole in its polling.
It takes a likeable leader to keep polling at a level that sees its most senior MPs and current Cabinet ministers return after just three years in power.
After continually choosing to put its electoral success in the hands of Luxon the caucus in some respects has only itself to blame.
Twice there have been confidence votes called on Luxon's leadership and twice he's stared his detractors down and stayed in the job despite eye-wateringly low net approval ratings.
Luxon's net approval score is unchanged in this poll, but that's not a celebration when it's a result of -23.7.
Choosing twice to recommit to Luxon has almost certainly hurt the party vote.
At the same time Luxon's approval is down the drain, Labour leader Chris Hipkins has turned his negative scores of the past two RNZ-Reid Research polls into a positive 5 percent.
That's backed up with him being ahead in the preferred prime minister stakes on 23 percent to Luxon's 17.
While National will be scratching its heads trying to work out how to turn the ship around with just over a week to go, Labour isn't in celebratory land either.
While it's cleared the twenties and hit 30 percent it would still need the Greens and Opportunity to form a government on these numbers.
Likewise with Opportunity holding the balance of power the centre-right bloc would also need Opportunity to get a majority - something Luxon continues to rule out as an option.
With the smaller parties increasing their share of the vote the leverage and influence they'll have in post-election coalition talks also grows.
It makes the promises from National and Labour on the campaign trail meaningless in some respects given the slate will be wiped clean at the negotiating table.
Opportunity looks to have charted a course through the middle putting itself in a strong powerbroker position on 7.2 percent as election day draws closer.
MPs in the coalition government continue to ridicule Opportunity, including National's Erica Stanford who this week called the party a "bunch of flakes" .
Attacks like those lay bare the true extent of the pressure National MPs are coming under.
